P.strongest_case: The knowledge-system-concept's own principle (§2.1: knowledge moves up, never down, and moves up only through one door) already commits the architecture to a single locus of truth per layer. Wiki/ pages are git-diffable, human-reviewable via status transitions (draft→reviewed→...), and queryable via wiki_lint.py + SQLite FTS5 — that is a complete, sufficient toolchain for a 680-document research corpus; nothing about scale or query complexity at this size requires graph-native traversal over page bodies. Mirroring Wiki content into new graph node/edge types would recreate, mechanism-for-mechanism, the exact failure documented in Plan/sessions/2026-09-11-learnings.md §1: an agent (there, a skill; here, a DSPy program) operating against a second, independently-mutable copy of a layer that already has one canonical location, silently drifting the moment either copy is edited without the other. The graph has no compaction/rebuild step tied to Wiki edits, so any mirrored copy is drift-by-construction, not drift-by-accident. Critically, this affirmation does not need to fight the existing ~220 capture_claim/NovelClaim writes to hold: those persist single verified claims (text + source_uri + domain enum) at the moment of *verification*, which is categorically different from persisting a Wiki page's exploratory body at the moment of *drafting*. The predicate's real boundary is granularity and gate-position, not 'anything research-related must never touch the graph' — and Phase 7's planned 'NovelClaims for verified T2 theory into the graph' is a confirming instance of exactly this channel, not an exception that needs squaring later. The rule is also the only one that gives Rule 0 a single, nameable door: D-xx decision → Canon/*.md edit → scripts/ingest_canon.py → graph → Codex/ re-render. Any second write path, however well-intentioned, reopens the ambiguity Rule 0 exists to close. Finally, this is the cheap-to-hold, expensive-to-reverse side of the decision: enforcing file-only Wiki persistence now costs nothing (it's the default absence of new graph schema); permitting graph mirroring now and walking it back after hundreds of Wiki/candidates and Wiki/concepts pages exist would require a data-migration and a schema deprecation the corpus does not yet owe.

reconstructions.fair_restatement: The apparent P/not-P conflict dissolves once 'Wiki content' is split into two non-overlapping kinds: whole-page prose/structure (never enters the graph — P holds) and atomic, source-cited claims independently derived from Canon/Sources material (already enter the graph via capture_claim, and will keep doing so under Phase 7 — not-P holds). That the NovelClaim schema is structurally incapable of holding page-length content 'by design, not convention' — inferred rather than confirmed against the graph driver's field constraints.

reconstructions.fair_restatement: The P/not-P question as posed is not yet truth-evaluable because it silently overloads two terms: 'the graph' (sometimes .agency/session.db, sometimes the file-based Wiki/graph/edges.jsonl) and 'Wiki content re-materialized' (sometimes raw draft prose, sometimes an already-verified capture_claim). A mechanical lint written straight off the predicate's current wording would either wrongly flag the sanctioned capture_claim channel or silently need an unstated exception; the predicate needs term-level disambiguation before it can be affirmed, rejected, or split.
unsupported_premises: That this term-inconsistency is actually load-bearing — i.e., has caused or would cause a real misfiled write or wrongly-flagged lint — rather than being a documentary imprecision a human reader resolves correctly on sight.
That readers would genuinely disagree on referents, inferred from the view's own unknowns list rather than from an observed multi-reader disagreement.

dissolution: P → neither: neither does not contest P's facts about capture_claim's sanctioned status; it reframes the question as ill-formed because 'the graph' and 'Wiki content' each denote two referents — a meta-level move, not a negation of P's content.

not-P → both: both uses the same evidentiary facts not-P cites (capture_claim traffic, Phase 7 plan) to show the apparent falsification of D-W2 is an equivocation between page-content and claim-content; once terms are split, no rejection of the underlying rule is needed.

not-P → neither: neither explicitly steps outside the P/not-P frame that not-P stays inside, arguing the verdict not-P reaches answers a question that is currently ill-posed rather than negating a well-posed one.
transformation: not-P's replacement_predicate converts the flat rejection into a positive, gated rule ('unverified research claims live only in Wiki/, but a claim that has cleared a named, checkable verification step may be written to the graph via the existing capture_claim path') — the object-level predicate survives, restated with an explicit gate, rather than being discarded outright.

both's patched_claim hardens P into two explicit clauses (page-body embargo + claim-channel carve-out with an explicit source_uri provenance requirement) — a refinement of the same predicate, not a dissolution of the underlying question.

neither's replacement_predicate transforms the single P/not-P binary into a three-channel model (draft prose in Wiki/ / Wiki-internal relations in edges.jsonl / verified claims via capture_claim / canon-locked facts via D-xx+ingest) keyed to artifact-kind and mutability — preserves the same underlying goal (keep unverified material out of author-locked graph state) while changing its structural shape from one boundary to three named ones.
cartography.arbiter_notes: All four corners agree on the same underlying facts (capture_claim's ~220 live writes, Phase 7's stated plan, the 2026-09-11 incident, edges.jsonl's existence) and diverge only in how they classify and bound them — which is itself evidence that this is a definitional/architectural decision, not a factual dispute, and squarely the kind of contested case CLAUDE.md flags as requiring a tetraframe run before being recorded as a D-xx, with the run itself never deciding. Of the four, both's page/claim ontology split is the strongest currently-available synthesis because it is the only corner that reconciles P's file-only intuition with not-P's correct observation that capture_claim already writes to the graph, without requiring either side's evidence to be wrong — but both's own stated unresolved_weaknesses (no enforcement mechanism yet; edges.jsonl's boundary status unaddressed) mean it should be adopted only after neither's disambiguation checks are run, and refined toward neither's three-channel framing and not-P's explicit-gate wording rather than left as an unenforced convention. Concretely, before any D-W2 text is finalized: (1) grep every use of 'graph' in Plan/wiki/knowledge-system-concept_2026-09-15.md and CLAUDE.md; (2) grep tools/kpwiki/*.py and graph-write call sites for capture_claim source_uri values, confirming none point into Wiki/; (3) inspect Wiki/graph/edges.jsonl's actual consumers for traversal vs. flat-list semantics; (4) put the capture_claim-scope question to the author directly via AskUserQuestion, since Rule 0 governs exactly this kind of ambiguous-scope decision. No premise beyond what the four corners themselves already assert or flag as unsupported has been introduced here.

transformed.transformed_predicate: Wiki/**/*.md (draft/exploratory source, concept, question and synthesis pages, plus the Wiki-internal relation ledger Wiki/graph/edges.jsonl) is the exclusive home for research-corpus *page-shaped* content: no script or verb ever copies a Wiki page's body, or a high-overlap paraphrase of one, into any .agency/session.db node or edge field, and no new graph node/edge type is minted to mirror a page's shape. Independently, and not in tension with that rule, atomic *claim-shaped* content — individual source-cited propositions captured via capability_novel_capture_claim / capture_idea, sourced directly from Canon/ or Sources/ material (never from a Wiki/ path) — is, and under Phase 7 will remain, a sanctioned, already-operating channel into .agency/session.db, gated by its existing domain-enum/source_uri contract. The sole door from either layer into author-locked Canon/graph narrative-fact status is an author-signed D-xx followed by scripts/ingest_canon.py; 'the graph' in this rule denotes .agency/session.db exclusively, and edges.jsonl is named explicitly as a distinct, Wiki-internal, file-based relation index, not a second graph.
transformed.transformed_frame: Reframe from a single medium prohibition ('Wiki content never touches the graph', yes/no) to a two-axis boundary: an artifact-KIND axis (whole page vs. atomic claim) crossed with a STRUCTURE-NAME axis (session.db vs. edges.jsonl). P was answering 'page vs. graph' and was right; not-P was answering 'has research content already reached session.db' and was also right, because it was implicitly answering about claims, not pages. Once the two axes are named separately, the apparent contradiction between P and not-P was never about facts — both corners cited the same ~220 capture_claim writes and the same Phase 7 text — it was two corners each silently resolving the same overloaded sentence differently. P* replaces the slogan with a partition: pages stay file-only by construction (never a violation to reconcile away), claims keep using the door they already use (never a rule to be silently overridden by), and the two structures previously both called 'the graph' get distinct names so a lint can be aimed at the actual overlap risk (a claim's text tracking too closely to one specific page) instead of at the medium itself.
survivors_from_p: No Wiki page body, verbatim or paraphrased, has ever been found copied into a graph node/edge field — this remains the actual, uncontested invariant, and the page-body embargo is retained as the operative rule, not diluted.

The 2026-09-11 drift-failure analogy is retained as the correct rationale for *that* embargo specifically (an independently-mutable second copy of page-shaped content drifting from its canonical home) — not stretched into a blanket 'graph bad, files good' argument, which not-P correctly showed doesn't hold at the claim-granularity.
D-xx + scripts/ingest_canon.py remains the sole, unambiguous door from Wiki/ into author-locked Canon/graph narrative-fact status — untouched by this reframing.

capture_claim/NovelClaim is retained as a sanctioned channel by design, not merely tolerated as an awkward exception — P's original framing of it as compatible turns out to be the correct reading once the kind-split is made explicit.
survivors_from_not_p: The demand that the rule explicitly name and reconcile with the ~220 live capture_claim writes, rather than describe the architecture as having 'one legal door' while a second live channel operates — this is now structurally built into the predicate instead of left as an unstated carve-out.

Phase 7's plan to keep writing verified T2-theory NovelClaims into the graph is treated as expected and pre-endorsed by the rule, not as a future conflict to be resolved later — not-P's warning that a literal zero-tolerance wording would be falsified by the project's own roadmap is fully absorbed.

The causal correction that file-vs-graph storage medium alone does not solve staleness — re-validation/invalidation discipline does — is preserved by scoping the embargo specifically to *page-shaped* content rather than implying that writing to session.db is inherently unsafe.

The observation that edges.jsonl already reinvents graph-shaped relation semantics in file form is preserved as a live risk, not dismissed — carried forward into boundary_conditions and operational_tests rather than resolved by assertion.
hidden_structure_from_both: The verb contract already enforces the page/claim split structurally: NovelClaim is schema-atomic (text+source_uri+domain, no page-shaped fields), so no existing script turns a Wiki page body into claim text — the split isn't aspirational, it's close to already-true.

capture_claim's source_uri, in every existing (~220) and Phase-7-planned invocation, is asserted to resolve to Canon/ or Sources/ material, never a Wiki/*.md path — meaning the graph never holds a claim *derived from* a Wiki page, only claims derived from the same upstream material a Wiki page also synthesizes.
This split lets Phase 7's planned T2-theory NovelClaim writes be read as a confirming instance of the existing channel rather than a looming exception that needs explaining away later.
dissolved_false_frame_from_neither: 'The graph' was treated as one referent when the corpus actually uses it for two structurally different things: .agency/session.db (immutable, author-locked, provenance-typed) and Wiki/graph/edges.jsonl (mutable, LLM-maintained, git-diffable, Wiki-internal). The P/not-P dispute partly evaporates once each sentence of D-W2 is pinned to one of the two.

'Wiki content re-materialized' was treated as one act when it actually covers two different acts: copying/paraphrasing a page's raw prose (the thing the 2026-09-11 drift analogy actually targets) versus recording an already-verified, source-cited, gate-passed atomic claim (capture_claim's actual operation). Collapsing these made P and not-P look like they were answering the same question when they were answering different halves of it.

The binary framing ('yes, Wiki content enters the graph' vs. 'no, it never does') is retired in favor of a per-artifact-kind rule, which is the only framing under which both cited fact-sets (zero page-body copies found; ~220 live claim writes) can be true without contradiction.
transformed.non_averaging_explanation: P* is not a midpoint between 'nothing from Wiki ever touches the graph' and 'plenty already does, so the rule is false' — it is a re-partition of the predicate along an axis (page vs. claim) that both corners' own evidence already supported but that P and not-P each applied only to half the cases. P is kept at full strength for pages (zero embargo violations found, unweakened), and not-P is kept at full strength for claims (the live channel is named and endorsed, not apologized for or hedged). Nothing is split down the middle: the page-body embargo is exactly as strict as P wanted it, and the claim channel is exactly as unrestricted as not-P observed it already to be. What changed is precision, not strength — the two overloaded terms neither identified ('the graph', 're-materialized') are pinned to single referents so the same strict rule can be stated without contradicting the same permissive fact.
operational_tests: Grep every occurrence of the word "graph" in Plan/wiki/knowledge-system-concept_2026-09-15.md and CLAUDE.md; confirm it is used to denote .agency/session.db exclusively, with edges.jsonl always referred to by a distinct name — if usage is inconsistent, the predicate's term-pinning needs to be written into the source docs, not just this decision.

Audit every existing and future capability_novel_capture_claim / capture_idea call site (tools/kpwiki/*.py once populated, plus the ~220 existing NovelClaims) for source_uri: PASS only if every value resolves to a Canon/ or Sources/ path; any Wiki/*.md source_uri is an immediate violation.

CI/lint: for every call_tool payload text going into a graph-write verb (capture_claim, capture_idea, create_codex_entry, any future create_*), run a text-overlap check (e.g. paragraph-level n-gram or embedding similarity above an explicit, documented threshold) against every Wiki/**/*.md page body; flag any high-overlap match as a probable page-body re-materialization rather than a distinct claim.

Inspect every consumer of Wiki/graph/edges.jsonl (wiki_lint.py and any DSPy program) to determine whether it supports only flat/lint-only reads or real relational/transitive traversal; document the finding explicitly in the D-W2 record so its status (Wiki-internal file structure, not a second graph) is settled rather than assumed.

AskUserQuestion to the author before finalizing D-W2: confirm capture_claim was always intended to be outside a page-embargo rule's scope, and confirm 'the graph' in that rule means session.db exclusively — per Rule 0, this is the kind of scope ambiguity that must be settled by the author, not inferred.
boundary_conditions: Holds only as long as capture_claim/NovelClaim's source_uri values in practice resolve to Canon/ or Sources/ paths and never to Wiki/*.md — this is currently asserted, not yet mechanically verified.

Holds only under the current NovelClaim schema (atomic text+source_uri+domain, no page-shaped fields); if the schema is ever widened to accept longer free text, the structural argument for the split weakens and needs re-auditing.

Holds only while Wiki/graph/edges.jsonl remains a flat, lint-only relation list; if it grows real transitive/programmatic traversal semantics, it should be explicitly reclassified (named as a second graph-shaped structure) rather than silently left ambiguous.

Applies specifically to the Wiki/ vs. .agency/session.db boundary for the research-corpus layer — does not itself govern other repo layers (Codex/, Manuscript/, Legacy/) or resolve unrelated provenance questions.
Remains provisional (per CLAUDE.md's tetraframe mandate) until recorded as an author-signed D-xx with this operational specificity — this synthesis does not itself constitute that sign-off.
failure_modes: The text-overlap/paraphrase threshold in the CI lint is either too loose (misses a genuine page-body copy reworded enough to slip through) or too tight (false-flags a legitimately independent claim that happens to echo page phrasing) — 'high-overlap paraphrase' is currently a judgment call, not a calibrated number, and needs a documented threshold plus test cases before it counts as mechanically checkable rather than aspirationally checkable.

A future tools/kpwiki/ script summarizes a Wiki page into a capture_claim call as a shortcut (e.g. 'just capture the page's conclusion as a claim') — structurally exactly what the split forbids, but nothing currently prevents an agent from doing it absent the lint existing.

edges.jsonl quietly accretes real relational query logic (e.g. a script starts resolving transitive supersession chains programmatically) without anyone re-classifying it, so the 'edges.jsonl is not a graph' half of the predicate becomes false by drift rather than decision — the same failure shape as the original 2026-09-11 incident, recurring one layer up.

The author's actual intent about capture_claim's scope (assumed here, not confirmed) turns out to differ from this reconstruction — e.g. they intended capture_claim itself to require a stronger Wiki-internal verification gate before firing, which would mean this synthesis under-specified the claim channel's own preconditions.

No enforcement exists yet for any version of this rule (true across all four original corners) — until the lint in operational_tests is actually written, compliance is discipline-based, and the rule could be silently violated in the gap between decision and implementation.
